info.title: What To Do
info.description:
Local backend of «What To Do». It reads public Telegram channels, public Instagram profiles and event websites, Claude turns posts into event cards
and merges the same event announced by several channels into one card.

**First run.** The app starts empty: add a city (`POST /cities`, the first one becomes active),
add sources (`POST /sources`): Telegram channels, Instagram profiles or websites, press refresh (`POST /refresh`) and poll `GET /refresh` until `running` is false.

**Active city.** Sources, the feed, places and refresh work with the active city only (`active_city_id` in settings).
Without a city these answer 409. Tags and the priority wish are shared by all cities; the card language is each city's own.

**Errors** come as `{"detail": "<text ready to show>"}`.

post.description:
Adds a public Telegram channel, a public Instagram profile or a website to the active city.
Its posts or events are read on the next refresh.

422: not a channel, profile or event page link, a bare name without the kind, the channel or profile is closed,
nothing is chosen to read from an Instagram profile, or the site cannot be read. 409: already added.

What adding the link would add: a channel's or an Instagram profile's title (with its number of pinned stories),
or a website's name, its event pages and a few examples.

422: the link is not a channel or profile, a bare name comes without the kind, the profile cannot be read,
or the site has no list of pages or no event markup.

extraction_prompt.title: Extraction Prompt
extraction_prompt.description: Instructions Claude gets for reading posts. Placeholders: {city}, {language}, {tags}, {fallback}
extraction_prompt.default:
You turn posts from Telegram channels and event pages of websites into event cards for a person who lives in {city} and looks for things to do in person.

For every post return the events and places it announces. Most posts announce nothing: return empty lists for them.

What to keep
- Offline events that take place in {city}. Drop online events, events in other cities, ads, giveaways, news and reports about events that already happened.
- A digest post that lists many events becomes one item per event.
- A place with no date goes to "places", never to "events".
- A follow-up about an event announced earlier is an item too: a post that adds details (update_kind "details"), moves it ("reschedule") or cancels it ("cancellation"), e.g. «Зачем идти на церемонию к Юле?» or «Сегодня лекции не будет». Name the event as the earlier announcement would. Resolve «сегодня», «завтра» and weekdays against the publication date; when the post gives no date at all, start_date is null. Only details and cancellations may go without a date.

Websites
- A website post is the facts of one event page: name, start, end, place, price, organizer, then the page's description. Its "channel" is the website: an afisha, never the event's organizer, so from_organizer is false.

Photos
- Each post lists its photos by index: "shows" says what the photo is, "text" is the text on it, transcribed word for word. Read them as part of the post: posters and event cards often carry the date, time, price, venue and the whole description.
- For every event give "photo": the index of its post's photo that shows that event.
- A poster shared by several events of a post, such as the poster of a lecture series, a festival or a programme, is the photo of every one of them.

Channels
- For every post list in "channels" each other Telegram channel it is forwarded from, links to (t.me/...) or mentions (@name), whatever the post is about, even when it announces no event.

The description language is {language}. Allowed tags: {tags}. If none fits, use exactly "{fallback}".
Each field's meaning is in the schema.

matching_prompt.title: Matching Prompt
matching_prompt.description: Instructions Claude gets for merging duplicates
matching_prompt.default:
You merge duplicate event announcements collected from several Telegram channels and websites.

You get existing event cards and new announcements. For every new announcement decide whether it describes the same real-world event as one of the existing cards, as one of the earlier new announcements, or neither.

Same event: the same happening at the same place on the same date, even when titles differ or are in different languages. Also the same: a post that reschedules, cancels or adds details to an event announced earlier (update_kind says so), and a single date of a recurring event that has a recurring card.
Not the same: different events at the same venue on the same day; the same show or tour on different dates; different sessions of a festival when each is its own event.

An announcement without a start_date is a follow-up its channel posted about one of its own events; the existing cards offered for it are that channel's. Pick the card it is about by title, description and venue; if none clearly fits, leave both fields null.

Never set both same_as_card and same_as_announcement.

photo_prompt.title: Photo Prompt
photo_prompt.description: Instructions Claude gets for transcribing post photos
photo_prompt.default:
You transcribe the photos of posts that announce events: posters, event cards, schedules, digests.

Every photo comes after its caption with its number. Return one item per photo. Each field's meaning is in the schema.
